text: Late collisions appear on one end of a link. What are the two possible causes?
choices: A duplex mismatch, or a segment that exceeds the maximum length
A routing loop or a spanning tree reconvergence
An MTU mismatch or a wrong VLAN
explanation: A late collision is one detected after the first 64 bytes, which by design should be impossible on a correctly configured segment. It means either the segment is longer than the standard permits, or one end is half duplex while the other is full — and in modern networks it is almost always the second.
